note: Real mods the runner puts through the whole modaccel loop on fresh clones. commit pins the run; --latest uses the head of branch instead. project selects a Gradle module (Stonecutter node). edit_file is the source file the stale-game check appends a comment to; empty picks the first Java file under src/main/java. setup_only entries stop after setup (no client: no --project on a multi-project build); nodes lists Gradle projects that each compile on their own (--project NODE). known_failures records an upstream failure by node with the exact error text it must show; a different error, or the node passing, is reported.

mods.name: F3Nope
mods.why_port: Upstream F3Nope declares minecraft ~1.20.1 in fabric.mod.json at every commit, so its own dev client refuses to load (head 50b7c70 on 1.21.6 fails with Incompatible mods found). Porting d65a225 (1.21.5) to 1.21.6 rewrites that range, which also puts port in the loop.

mods.name: Diorama (no --project)
mods.setup_only: no --project on a multi-project build: the evaluated model of every project is compared, then every node compiles on its own; the client task is ambiguous by design

:1.21.6.reason: Upstream Diorama at this commit: src/gametest/java/dev/diorama/test/DioramaClientTest.java calls WorldVersion.getPackVersion(PackType), which this node's game does not have, so :compileGametestJava fails. Same error on Windows, Linux and macOS in CI; not a modaccel failure.

:1.21.8-neoforge.reason: Upstream Diorama at this commit: src/gametest/java/dev/diorama/test/DioramaClientTest.java calls WorldVersion.getPackVersion(PackType), which this node's game does not have, so :compileGametestJava fails. Same error on Windows, Linux and macOS in CI; not a modaccel failure.
